n096555b2422.s: Which of the following is excluded from the social indicators of poverty?
n096555b2422.x: Illiteracy, malnutrition, poor health care and lack of safe water and sanitation are social indicators of poverty; size of the house is not one.

ne0c5e394c87.s: Which poverty estimation method used CPI-AL for rural areas and CPI-IW for urban areas?
ne0c5e394c87.x: The Lakdawala methodology kept the calorie base, used state-specific poverty lines and applied CPI-AL for rural and CPI-IW for urban areas.

nindian-society-11-13.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: S.R. Hashim Expert Group – Rural BPL census
N.C. Saxena Expert Group – Rural BPL census methodology
Rangarajan Committee – Chaired by Bimal Jalan
N.C. Saxena Expert Group – Urban BPL households
nindian-society-11-13.x: N.C. Saxena dealt with the rural BPL census and S.R. Hashim with urban BPL identification; C. Rangarajan chaired the Rangarajan Committee.

nb0a68a458d3.s: Under the Current Daily Status, activity is recorded for:
o: Only the day of the survey
Each day of the reference week
nb0a68a458d3.x: Current Daily Status records activity for each day of the reference week, not only the day of the survey.

n35eef38a3a5.s: DAY-NRLM (2011) was a restructuring of which scheme?
n35eef38a3a5.x: DAY-NRLM restructured SGSY, an SHG-based self-employment scheme, not JRY, which was a wage-employment scheme.

n85c0c1f7d66.s: NREGA was renamed the Mahatma Gandhi NREGA (MGNREGA) on:
n85c0c1f7d66.x: NREGA was enacted in 2005, came into force on 2 February 2006 and was renamed MGNREGA on 2 October 2009.

n1d65d71dd8b.s: Which one of the following rights is absent from the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?
o: Right to an adequate standard of living
n1d65d71dd8b.x: The UDHR includes dignity, liberty, equality, life, an adequate standard of living and education, but not a right to universal basic income.

nac54125d23c.s: The Optional Protocol to the ICESCR was adopted in:
nac54125d23c.x: The ICESCR Optional Protocol was adopted in 2008; 1976 is when the two Covenants entered into force.

nad699a3ccd7.s: Which core UN human rights treaty has India not signed?
nad699a3ccd7.x: India has not signed the CMW; it ratified CRPD in 2007 and signed CPED in 2007 without ratifying it.

nabf543fbb3e.s: The UN Human Rights Council, formed in 2006, replaced the:
o: Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights
nabf543fbb3e.x: The Human Rights Council was formed in 2006 as the successor to the UN Commission on Human Rights; it is based in Geneva.

n00b81ec5114.s: A member of the UN Human Rights Council can serve at most how many consecutive terms?
n00b81ec5114.x: Members are elected by the UNGA for three-year terms and may serve at most two consecutive terms.

n3b47a2ccea5.s: The UN General Assembly recognised the Right to Water and Sanitation on:
n3b47a2ccea5.x: The Right to Water and Sanitation was recognised on 28 July 2010; the Right to Development came in 1986 and the environment right on 28 July 2022.

ne032162ef74.s: Which of the following pairs about GANHRI accreditation is correctly matched?
o: 'A' status – Partly compliant with the Paris Principles
'B' status – Fully compliant with the Paris Principles
Sub-Committee on Accreditation – Accredits NHRIs for GANHRI
'A' status – Non-compliant with the Paris Principles
ne032162ef74.x: GANHRI accredits NHRIs through its Sub-Committee on Accreditation; 'A' means fully and 'B' partly compliant.

nindian-polity-2-7.s: Article 40 of the Constitution, on village panchayats, falls under:
o: Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV)
nindian-polity-2-7.x: Article 40 is a Directive Principle in Part IV, while Articles 14 and 32 are Fundamental Rights in Part III.

nindian-polity-43-15.s: The National Green Tribunal Act was enacted in:
nindian-polity-43-15.x: The National Green Tribunal Act dates from 2010, not 2013.

nindian-society-32-17.s: Under the UDHR, the right to social security is classed as a/an:
nindian-society-32-17.x: Work, education, social security and health are economic and social rights in the UDHR.

nindian-polity-2-3.s: Which Article of the Constitution makes laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights void?
nindian-polity-2-3.x: Article 13 makes laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights void, which is the basis of judicial review.

n34d18a7a9d7.s: The advice of the National Human Rights Commission to the Government is:
o: Binding on both Union and States
n34d18a7a9d7.x: NHRC advice is non-binding on the Government; the NHRC is a statutory body.

n809609707a0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about human rights and Fundamental Rights in India?
o: Every Fundamental Right is a human right
Not every human right is a Fundamental Right
The right to vote is a statutory right
The right to vote is a Fundamental Right under Part III
n809609707a0.x: The right to vote in India is only a statutory right, not a Fundamental Right; Fundamental Rights are a part of the wider body of human rights.

nindian-polity-22-53.s: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 came into force in:
nindian-polity-22-53.x: The Domestic Violence Act was enacted in 2005 and came into force in 2006 (26 October 2006).

new.s: Being poor compared with others in the same society is called:
new.x: Relative poverty means being poor in comparison with others in the same society; absolute poverty is spending below a fixed poverty line.

new.s: India's official poverty line is based on:
new.x: India's official poverty line is consumption-based, set by Monthly Per Capita Consumption Expenditure (MPCE), not income.

new.s: The Y.K. Alagh Task Force on poverty estimation was set up in:
new.x: The Alagh Task Force (1979) used a calorie-only norm of 2,400 rural and 2,100 urban.

new.s: According to the Tendulkar methodology, poverty in India in 2011-12 was:
new.x: The Tendulkar line put poverty at 21.9% in 2011-12; 37.2% was its 2004-05 figure and 2.3% the 2023-24 figure.

new.s: In October 2025, which body updated the Rangarajan poverty line using HCES 2022-23?
new.x: In October 2025 the RBI updated the Rangarajan line using HCES 2022-23 and a poverty-line-basket price index.

new.s: Which survey is the standard for unemployment data in India?
new.x: The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) of the NSO is the standard for unemployment data (APPSC Group 2, 2025 key).

new.s: Under PLFS, the Current Weekly Status uses a reference period of:
new.x: Current Weekly Status covers the 7 days before the survey; usual status covers the reference year.

new.s: The NSO's Household Consumption Expenditure Survey is conducted about every:
new.x: The HCES is conducted about every 5 years, and its MPCE data set the poverty line.

new.s: The National Multidimensional Poverty Index is built by NITI Aayog with:
new.x: The National MPI is built by NITI Aayog with UNDP and OPHI.

new.s: As per NITI MPI 2023, the multidimensional poverty headcount of Andhra Pradesh was:
new.x: AP's headcount was 6.06% (rank 9th), well below India's 14.96%; Bihar recorded 33.76%.

new.s: Disguised unemployment, where extra workers add near-zero output, is mainly found in:
new.x: Disguised unemployment means more workers than needed, with near-zero marginal productivity, mainly on family farms in agriculture.

new.s: Unemployment caused by a mismatch between workers' skills and the jobs available is:
new.x: Structural unemployment is a long-term mismatch between skills and available jobs.

new.s: Unemployment arising from a fall in labour demand during an economic slowdown is:
new.x: Cyclical unemployment follows the trade cycle, rising when labour demand falls in a slowdown.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (unemployment type – predominant area) is correctly matched?
new.x: Educated and frictional unemployment are urban; disguised and seasonal unemployment are mainly in agriculture.

new.s: PMEGP (2008) was formed by merging:
new.x: PMEGP merged PMRY and REGP and gives a credit-linked subsidy through KVIC; JRY merged NREP and RLEGP.

new.s: DWCRA (1982-83) was a sub-scheme of IRDP meant to reach:
new.x: DWCRA was a sub-scheme of IRDP so that benefits reached rural women directly; TRYSEM trained rural youth.

new.s: Under MGNREGA, at least what share of the workers must be women?
new.x: At least one-third of MGNREGA workers must be women, not half.

new.s: Under MGNREGA, if work is not provided within how many days of demand is an unemployment allowance due?
new.x: If work is not given within 15 days of demand, an unemployment allowance is payable.

new.s: NREGA came into force on 2 February 2006, starting in which district?
new.x: NREGA first came into force on 2 February 2006 starting from Anantapur district in Andhra Pradesh.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about MGNREGA:
1. Social audits are held by the Gram Sabha.
2. The right to work it guarantees is a Fundamental Right in Part III.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Gram Sabhas hold social audits; MGNREGA follows the Directive Principles, and the right to work is not in Part III.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a practice leading to social exclusion?
o: Denied access to land and water
new.x: Untouchability, segregation and denied access to land, water and jobs lead to exclusion; MGNREGA wage employment is a policy response to it.

new.s: Which social group has the highest incidence of poverty in India?
new.x: Scheduled Tribes have the highest poverty, followed by Scheduled Castes (ST > SC > others).

new.s: As per NITI MPI 2023, which State had the lowest multidimensional poverty?
new.x: Kerala recorded the lowest MPI poverty and Bihar (33.76%) the highest.

new.s: As per 2025-26 data, informal employment in rural Andhra Pradesh stood at:
new.x: Rural informal employment in AP was 62.3%; 47.5% is AP's LFPR and 64.3% is social protection coverage.

new.s: India's social protection coverage rose from 22% in 2016 to what in 2025?
new.x: Social protection coverage rose from 22% (2016) to 64.3% (2025).

new.s: Gig workers form roughly what share of India's workforce (2025-26)?
new.x: Gig workers make up 2%+ of the workforce; migrant, casual and unorganised workers have little social security.

new.s: Human rights are best described as rights that are:
o: Granted by the State to citizens
Inherent and inalienable to every human being
Available only to citizens of UN members
new.x: Human rights are inherent and inalienable rights held simply because one is human, resting on human dignity.

new.s: In Karel Vasak's classification, third-generation human rights are linked to the ideal of:
new.x: First, second and third generations correspond to liberty, equality and fraternity (solidarity).

new.s: Which of the following is a third-generation (collective) human right?
new.x: Third-generation rights are collective: healthy environment, development and peace; work is second-generation, speech and fair trial first.

new.s: Who chaired the committee that drafted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?
new.x: Eleanor Roosevelt chaired the UDHR drafting; Karel Vasak proposed the generations and Peter Benenson founded Amnesty.

new.s: Human Rights Day on 10 December was set by UNGA resolution 423(V) in:
new.x: UNGA resolution 423(V) of 1950 fixed 10 December as Human Rights Day.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the UDHR:
1. It was adopted on 10 December 1948.
2. It has a Preamble and 30 articles.
3. It is a legally binding treaty.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The UDHR was adopted on 10 December 1948 with a Preamble and 30 articles, but it is not a treaty and not legally binding.

new.s: Freedom of expression is protected under which Article of the ICCPR?
new.x: ICCPR Article 19 covers expression; Article 17 covers privacy, Article 14 fair trial and Article 24 child rights.

new.s: The ICESCR entered into force on:
new.x: The ICESCR came into force on 3 January 1976, before the ICCPR (23 March 1976); both were adopted on 16 December 1966.

new.s: India has been a party to the ICCPR since:
new.x: India is a party to the ICCPR since 1979 but has not signed its First Optional Protocol.

new.s: India's status with respect to the Convention against Torture (CAT) is:
new.x: India signed CAT in 1997 but has not ratified it; CAT and CPED are signed but not ratified, and CMW is not signed.

new.s: India ratified CEDAW in:
new.x: India ratified CEDAW in 1993; CEDAW itself dates from 1979.

new.s: Which convention did India accede to on 11 December 1992?
new.x: India acceded to the Convention on the Rights of the Child (CRC) on 11 December 1992.

new.s: How many members does the UN Human Rights Council have?
new.x: The Human Rights Council has 47 members elected by the UNGA for three-year terms.

new.s: How many seats does the Asia-Pacific group hold in the UN Human Rights Council?
new.x: Asia-Pacific and Africa hold 13 seats each; Latin America 8, Western Europe and Others 7, Eastern Europe 6.

new.s: A UN Human Rights Council member can be suspended for gross violations by what UNGA vote?
new.x: A two-thirds vote of the UNGA can suspend a member for gross violations.

new.s: Special rapporteurs under the Human Rights Council's special procedures are:
o: Paid UN staff of the OHCHR
Judges of the International Court of Justice
new.x: Special rapporteurs are unpaid independent experts on a theme or country under the HRC special procedures.

new.s: The Universal Periodic Review, held in cycles of about 4.5 years, began in:
new.x: The UPR, a peer review of every UN member's record, has run since 2008 in cycles of about 4.5 years.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a content of the Paris Principles?
o: Reliance on the executive for inquiries
new.x: The Paris Principles require independence, pluralism, resources and powers to investigate, not reliance on the executive.

new.s: Human Rights Watch is based in:
new.x: Human Rights Watch is New York-based; Amnesty International was founded in London.

new.s: The UN Human Rights Prize, given usually every five years, has been awarded since:
new.x: The UNGA has given the UN Human Rights Prize since 1968, usually every five years.

new.s: Amnesty International was founded in 1961 by:
new.x: Amnesty International was founded in London in 1961 by British lawyer Peter Benenson; it won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1977.

new.s: Amnesty International received the Nobel Peace Prize in:
new.x: Amnesty International won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1977; it was founded in 1961.

new.s: Article 14 of the Indian Constitution corresponds to which Article of the UDHR?
new.x: Article 14 (equality before law) matches UDHR Article 7; Article 21 matches Article 3 and Article 32 matches Article 8.

new.s: Article 32 of the Constitution (constitutional remedies) parallels which UDHR Article?
new.x: Article 32, called the 'Heart and Soul' by Ambedkar, parallels UDHR Article 8.

new.s: Which Fundamental Right is available only to citizens?
new.x: Article 19's six freedoms are for citizens only; Articles 14, 20, 21, 23 and 25-28 also cover foreigners.

new.s: The right to a speedy trial was read into Article 21 in:
new.x: Hussainara Khatoon (1979) gave speedy trial; Hoskot legal aid, Olga Tellis livelihood, Francis Coralie dignity.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (right under Article 21 – case) is correctly matched?
new.x: Subhash Kumar (1991) gave a clean environment; privacy came from Puttaswamy (2017), livelihood from Olga Tellis, legal aid from Hoskot.

new.s: The right to privacy was held part of Article 21 in which case?
new.x: K.S. Puttaswamy (2017) recognised privacy under Article 21; D.K. Basu laid down arrest safeguards.

new.s: Which Directive Principle provides for maternity relief?
new.x: Article 42 provides humane conditions of work and maternity relief; Article 43 is the living wage.

new.s: A Special Public Prosecutor for a Human Rights Court must be an advocate of at least:
new.x: Section 31 of the PHRA lets the State Government specify an advocate of 7 years' practice as Special Public Prosecutor.

new.s: Under the PHRA, 1993, the Chairperson of a State Human Rights Commission is appointed by the:
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
new.x: The NHRC is appointed by the President and the SHRC by the Governor; the selection committees are headed by the PM and CM.

new.s: Under the PHRA, 'public servant' has the meaning given in Section 21 IPC, now replaced by:
new.x: Section 2(1)(m) of the PHRA defines public servant as in Section 21 IPC, now Section 2(28) of the BNS from 1 July 2024.

new.s: After the 2019 amendment, the NHRC Chairperson can be a former Chief Justice of India or a former:
o: Chief Justice of a High Court
new.x: The 2019 amendment allows a former CJI or a Supreme Court judge to chair the NHRC; any HC judge is eligible only for the SHRC chair.

new.s: The 2019 amendment reduced the term of NHRC Chairperson and members from 5 years to:
new.x: The term was cut from 5 to 3 years (or age 70), and reappointment is allowed.

new.s: Which of the following was added as a deemed member of the NHRC by the 2019 amendment?
new.x: The 2019 amendment added the chairs of the NCBC and NCPCR and the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities as deemed members.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the 2019 amendment to the PHRA:
1. Human-rights members of the NHRC rose from 2 to 3, one being a woman.
2. Any High Court judge can now chair an SHRC.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: members rose from 2 to 3 including a woman, and an SHRC chair can now be any HC judge as well.

new.s: Under the Manual Scavengers Act, 2013, which is prohibited?
o: All sanitation work by local bodies
new.x: The 2013 Act bars sewer cleaning without protective gear and requires local bodies to survey and build sanitary latrines within 3 years.
